parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Define electric potential at a point.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Two isolated charged metal spheres X and Y are near to each other in a vacuum. The centres of the spheres are 1.2m apart, as shown in Fig. 5.1.

[[fig:f1]]

Point P is on the line joining the centres of spheres X and Y and is at a variable distance *x* from the centre of X.

Fig. 5.2 shows the variation with *x* of the total electric potential *V* due to the two spheres.

[[fig:f2]]

State three conclusions that may be drawn about the spheres from Fig. 5.2. The conclusions may be qualitative or quantitative.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
A proton is held at rest on the line joining the centres of the spheres in (b) at the position where *x* = 0.60m.

The proton is released.

Describe and explain, without calculation, the subsequent motion of the proton.

figures.caption: Fig. 5.1
figures.alt: Two spheres labelled X and Y are shown with point P between their centres, with distances x and 1.2m indicated.

figures.caption: Fig. 5.2
figures.alt: A graph of electric potential V against x / m has a U-shaped curve, falling to a minimum before rising steeply.
